summary.text: Barry Moore is the Republican nominee for Alabama's open U.S. Senate seat and a sitting U.S. Representative. A farm-raised Enterprise businessman and Army National Guard veteran, he served in the Alabama House of Representatives from 2010 to 2018 and has been in the U.S. House since 2021, serving on the Agriculture and Judiciary committees. He won the June 16, 2026 Republican primary runoff for the Senate nomination.

paragraphs.text: Barry Moore was born and raised on a family farm in Coffee County, Alabama, according to his official House biography.

He earned a B.S. in agricultural science from Auburn University in 1992 and, after high school, served six years in the Alabama National Guard and Reserves; Ballotpedia lists service in the U.S. Army National Guard.

After college he worked in the animal pharmaceutical industry before returning to Enterprise, Alabama, to start Hopper-Moore Inc., an industrial waste hauling company that his official biography says has also been an Alabama general contractor for more than two decades.

Moore was recruited to run for the Alabama House of Representatives in 2010 and served District 91 for eight years (2010-2018), including as chairman of the Military and Veterans Affairs Committee and vice chair of the Small Business and Commerce Committee.
He was elected to the U.S. House for Alabama's 2nd District in 2020 and re-elected in 2022.

After the 2023 redistricting placed him and fellow Republican incumbent Jerry Carl in the same district, he defeated Carl in the March 5, 2024 Republican primary (51.7% to 48.3%) and won the general election for the renumbered 1st District.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) Moore sits on the House Agriculture Committee and the Judiciary Committee; earlier terms included Veterans' Affairs (2021-2022). He is not seeking re-election to the House.
He advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary to a June 16 runoff and defeated Jared Hudson for the Senate nomination.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Heather, who is also his business partner, have four children and are members of Hillcrest Baptist Church in Enterprise.
